scenarioStory.history: Bystanders report the patient was stabbed once in the left proximal thigh during an altercation approximately 8 minutes ago. She is conscious, anxious, and reports she 'can't stop the bleeding' despite holding a t-shirt against the wound. Blood is pooling rapidly on the pavement beneath her leg.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 52-year-old female with an actively bleeding stab wound to the left proximal thigh. A bystander is holding direct pressure, but blood continues to spurt from beneath the dressing. Patient is alert but anxious, pale, and tachycardic. → Tourniquet applied: Crew applies a commercial tourniquet proximal to the wound, marks the application time, establishes IV access, and gives TXA and a fluid bolus targeting the trauma resuscitation blood pressure goal. → Bleeding controlled, TXA and fluids given: Hemorrhage is controlled with the tourniquet in place, TXA and a fluid bolus have been given, and the crew initiates rapid transport within the scene time goal while reassessing serially en route.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Stab wound to left thigh with brisk, spurting bleeding

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 52-year-old female with an actively bleeding stab wound to the left proximal thigh. A bystander is holding direct pressure, but blood continues to spurt from beneath the dressing. Patient is alert but anxious, pale, and tachycardic.
relatedChecklist: Apply commercial tourniquet 2-3 inches proximal to wound until bleeding stops and distal pulse eliminated
Be prepared to apply a second tourniquet proximal to the first if bleeding continues, given the proximal thigh location
Mark and document tourniquet application time prominently on patient and in the patient care report
Establish IV access and give TXA, within 3 hours of injury with signs of hemorrhagic shock
Give 500 mL crystalloid bolus targeting SBP 90 mmHg since blood products unavailable

scenarioEvents.name: Tourniquet applied
scenarioEvents.description: Crew applies a commercial tourniquet proximal to the wound, marks the application time, establishes IV access, and gives TXA and a fluid bolus targeting the trauma resuscitation blood pressure goal.
relatedChecklist: Minimize scene time and initiate rapid transport to trauma center, goal under 10 minutes
Reassess tourniquet and vitals frequently en route without removing the tourniquet or dressing

scenarioEvents.name: Bleeding controlled, TXA and fluids given
scenarioEvents.description: Hemorrhage is controlled with the tourniquet in place, TXA and a fluid bolus have been given, and the crew initiates rapid transport within the scene time goal while reassessing serially en route.

scenarioEvents.name: Tourniquet delayed, direct pressure only
scenarioEvents.description: The crew continues with direct pressure and a pressure dressing alone despite ongoing brisk arterial bleeding, delaying the tourniquet. The patient's bleeding continues and perfusion worsens.
relatedChecklist: Recognize direct pressure has failed; apply commercial tourniquet 2-3 inches proximal to wound immediately

scenarioEvents.name: Tourniquet loosened for pain
scenarioEvents.description: The crew loosens the tourniquet in response to the patient's pain complaints, against explicit protocol guidance. Bleeding resumes and perfusion worsens.
relatedChecklist: Retighten tourniquet immediately; do not loosen for pain, treat pain with analgesics instead
